summary: The new route.ts is architecturally sound and correctly reuses the codebase's established requireAuthOrApiKey/requireRoleOrScope + buildCapabilityTree conventions (verified against the sibling /api/v1/projexa/capability-tree/route.ts and /api/capability-tree/route.ts): orgId always comes from the authenticated context (buildCapabilityTree internally wraps withTenantContext keyed off that same orgId), never from the request, so there is no cross-tenant leak vector, and the construction_intelligence branch filter correctly matches the key emitted by buildConstructionNodes() to avoid duplicating the sibling route's ownership. However, the new test file's mockTree() helper calls mock.module("@/lib/services/capability-tree-service", () => ({ buildCapabilityTree })), which replaces that module's exports process-wide for the rest of the bun test run (documented, and explicitly worked around elsewhere in this same repo -- see the comment in src/app/api/v1/reports/catalog/route.test.ts about exactly this Bun gotcha). Because the factory omits buildConstructionNodes, markDeterministic, and the CapabilityNode/CapabilityInputField types, any later-running test file that imports those from the same resolved file -- concretely, src/lib/services/capability-tree-service.test.ts, which does `import { markDeterministic } from "./capability-tree-service"` and calls it directly at runtime -- would receive undefined and crash with a TypeError once mock.module's override is in effect. Given default alphabetical test discovery (app/... sorts before lib/...), this route's test.ts runs first in a full `bun test` invocation, making the collision the default ordering, not an edge case.
issues: src/app/api/v1/projexa/module-chain/route.test.ts's mockTree() factory (`mock.module("@/lib/services/capability-tree-service", () => ({ buildCapabilityTree }))`) strips every other export of that module for the remainder of the bun test process, breaking src/lib/services/capability-tree-service.test.ts's direct, real import and call of markDeterministic() -- a regression of an existing, previously-passing test file, and exactly the class of bug this repo's own reports/catalog/route.test.ts comment already documents and works around by including all real exports in its mock factory. Fix: spread the real module (e.g. `const actual = await import("@/lib/services/capability-tree-service"); mock.module(..., () => ({ ...actual, buildCapabilityTree }))`) or otherwise include buildConstructionNodes/markDeterministic passthroughs before merging.
